items.prompt: By the end of this year, the firm ___ its profits.

explanation.en: By + a future time shows completion before it: future perfect.

optionNotes.en: Correct: completed before the end of the year.
By the end of this year looks forward to a future point, so the present perfect does not work: use will have + past participle.
The present simple does not fit a prediction of completion.

items.prompt: Don't call after eight. We ___ on the plane to Delhi.

explanation.en: An action in progress at a future moment: future continuous.

optionNotes.en: Correct: in progress at a future moment.
The future perfect would mean the sitting is finished before eight.
The present simple does not fit a future moment.

items.prompt: 'Could I borrow your drill?' 'Sure, I ___ it until Sunday, so help yourself.'

explanation.en: The future continuous says what will be happening, or not happening, at that time.

optionNotes.en: Correct: not in use over a future period.
The future perfect would mean completion before a point, not a period.
The present simple does not fit a future arrangement here.

items.prompt: By the time the exam begins, I ___ all my notes twice.

explanation.en: By the time + a count of completed actions: future perfect.
explanation.es: By the time + acción completada: future perfect.

optionNotes.en: Will read does not show completion before then.
Correct: completed before the exam begins.
The future continuous would mean the reading is in progress.

items.prompt: By next March, I ___ in this company for exactly ten years.

explanation.en: By + a future time with a total period: future perfect.
explanation.es: By + momento futuro con periodo total: future perfect.

optionNotes.en: Correct: total period completed by a future point.
The past simple cannot refer to a future point.
The present simple does not show completion by next March.
